text.home.about.p1: Hello — I'm Ricky Jin(金睿杰), a senior at Shanghai High School International Division(SHSID). My week usually splits three ways: chasing a research question, rehearsing a scene, and running sprints on a pitch that has seen better weather.
text.home.contact.text: If you'd like a fuller research portfolio, a full video of performance, or just to have a chill chat with me, my inbox is open.
text.athletics.lede: 14 years of soccer, started as striker and finally arrived at center back. Defense is geometry and anticipation — which is, more or less, the same thing I do with data.
text.theater.t10.role: Explaining the script to cast members while in a wheelchair
text.theater.g3.note: Acted in 2 shows with 600+ audiences. I researched 1920s-30s Shanghai with SJTU historians. The performance was shortlisted for French Embassy's Grand Prix France-Chine 2026
text.theater.lede: Nine productions, on stage and behind it. Theater is where I can truly be myself.
text.theater.g4.p1: Working an audience teaches you to read a room — fast.
text.theater.g4.p2: Performance is not just about perfectly following the script, but to naturally adapt to circumstances.
text.theater.g4.p3: Acting is to try different lives that you never get to experience.
text.service.other1.title: Urban Aid Alliance Online
text.service.hospital.text: Since summer 2024, I started to actively volunteer in Jiahui International Hospital. Every month, I participate in different fields of work for 3 hours, including lobby guidance, vaccine support, companionship for children.
text.service.xishan.p2: I taught English through alphabet-guessing games, taught basic soccer skills, and directed the students' first-ever play, The Little Girl Who Sold Charcoal. Watching shy observers become confident performers taught me more than any lesson I had planned. In the forests, the students became teachers, showing me how to identify the wild mushrooms that grew there.
text.service.xishan.quote: "There's a bigger world out there, and I want to see it for myself." - Luo
text.service.xishan.p1: In the summer of 2024, I arrived in Xishan Township, Eryuan, in the mountains of Yunnan — and the reality of rural education hit me hard. Thirty-two students shared a dormitory smaller than 40 square meters; the entire school owned three aging projectors; 80% of the students had never once left their county.
text.service.xishan.p3: One eight-day trip has grown into a multi-school alliance spanning Shanghai and Nanjing, bringing together volunteers from international and local schools. The curriculum now runs from English, history, and sports to math, chess, and paper quilling, and our fundraising campaigns have delivered over $10,000 in funds and supplies.
text.service.xishan.title: Beyond Mountains: A Three-Year Journey with Xi Shan Students
text.service.lede: Every summer since 2024, I have gone back to the same mountain classroom. Service, for me, has never been a line on a list — it is the place my passion and my teaching actually meet.
text.service.other1.text: Since fall 2024, I have led the UAA Online education program for students in rural Yunnan. I coordinated bi-weekly sessions and maintained the digital infrastructure for our online classroom, ensuring a stable and accessible learning environment.
text.service.other2.title: Theatre Festival for the Blind
text.service.other2.text: 2026 winter, I founded an special interschool performance for 20 visually impaired audience members. We adapted scripts, staging, and choreography for the people.

text.research.p1.title: Hybrid CNN Features and a Zero-Label Composition Score
text.research.p1.abstract: Traditional calligraphy learning relies heavily on costly mentor feedback, and existing automated systems typically evaluate only individual characters, ignoring overall page layout (zhangfa). To address this gap, we propose an end-to-end scoring pipeline that runs in real-time on standard laptops. Our approach combines a ResNet-18 model with handcrafted features for character-level assessment (achieving a MAE of 0.35) and a novel zero-label, unsupervised model for composition scoring based on geometric metrics. The final score integrates both dimensions via a weighted formula. Validated through synthetic perturbation tests, this lightweight system provides comprehensive, dual-dimension feedback for self-directed learners without professional instructors. Notably, we also report the failure of test-time augmentation due to direction-sensitive features.
